policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Article on αὕτη only; ASV 'This was the first enrolment' renders the demonstrative identically with or without ἡ.
ἑαυτοῦ and ἰδίαν are both rendered 'his own' in ASV 'every one to his own city'; the English does not distinguish the possessives.
ASV reads 'Mary, who was betrothed to him' with no rendering of γυναικί; the RP reading would require 'his betrothed wife'.
ASV 'laid him in a manger' is indefinite, rendering the anarthrous ἐν φάτνῃ; the arthrous RP reading would give 'in the manger'.
ASV 'And an angel of the Lord stood by them' has no 'behold'; ASV renders ἰδού where it stands (2:25 'And behold, there was a man').
Article on the predicate σημεῖον only; ASV 'this is the sign unto you' renders a definite predicate noun with or without τό.
ASV joins the two participles with 'and': 'wrapped in swaddling clothes, and lying in a manger'; the RP omission leaves no conjunction to render.
ASV 'the heavenly host' renders the adjective οὐρανίου and the genitive οὐρανοῦ alike; English regularly turns such a genitive attributive.

ASV 'peace among men in whom he is well pleased' with the gloss 'Greek men of good pleasure' renders the genitive εὐδοκίας; the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read peace, good pleasure among men' puts the nominative εὐδοκία in the margin.
ASV reads simply 'the shepherds said one to another' with no rendering of οἱ ἄνθρωποι ('the men').
ASV 'said one to another' fits imperfect ἐλάλουν and aorist εἶπον alike; the only note here is classed alternative_rendering and does not decide a reading.
ASV 'they made known' renders ἐγνώρισαν and the compound διεγνώρισαν identically.
Μαρία and Μαριάμ are both rendered 'Mary'; the ASV spelling does not distinguish the Greek forms.
ASV 'in the law of the Lord' is definite either way: νόμῳ κυρίου is definite by its genitive without τῷ.
Word order only; ASV 'there was a man in Jerusalem' does not reflect the position of ἦν.
ASV 'before he had seen the Lord's Christ' renders πρὶν ἤ, πρὶν ἄν and πρὶν ἢ ἄν identically; the particles have no separate English exponent.
ASV 'into his arms' supplies the possessive that Greek carries by the article τὰς ἀγκάλας, so 'his' does not require αὐτοῦ.
ASV reads 'his father and his mother', not 'Joseph and his mother'; the proper name of the RP reading is absent.
ASV 'his mother' supplies the possessive the article ἡ μήτηρ already implies in this context, so it does not require αὐτοῦ.
ASV 'yea and a sword shall pierce' renders the καὶ … δέ combination; without δέ the conjunction would be a plain 'and'.
Word order only; ASV 'having lived with a husband seven years' does not reflect the position of ἔτη.
ASV 'a widow even unto fourscore and four years' renders ἕως; ὡς would give an approximation ('about fourscore and four years').
ASV 'departed not from the temple' requires 'from' in English whether or not ἀπό stands before τοῦ ἱεροῦ.
ASV 'And coming up at that very hour she gave thanks' takes 'she' from the verb; an added αὕτη has no separate exponent in the English.
ASV 'gave thanks unto God' renders θεῷ; the RP κυρίῳ would give 'unto the Lord'.
ASV 'the redemption of Jerusalem' renders the bare genitive; the RP ἐν would give 'redemption in Jerusalem'.
πάντα and ἅπαντα are both rendered 'all things'; the English does not distinguish the strengthened form.
ASV 'they returned into Galilee' renders ἐπέστρεψαν and ὑπέστρεψαν identically.
ASV 'into Galilee' leaves the article on the proper name unrendered, as English requires; τήν is not distinguished.
ASV 'waxed strong, filled with wisdom' has no rendering of πνεύματι; the RP reading would give 'waxed strong in spirit'.
ASV 'they went up after the custom of the feast' renders the genitive absolute alike for present ἀναβαινόντων and aorist ἀναβάντων.
ASV 'they went up after the custom of the feast' names no destination; the RP addition would require 'to Jerusalem'.
ASV 'his parents knew it not' renders the plural οἱ γονεῖς; the RP reading would give 'Joseph and his mother knew not'.
Word order only; ASV 'supposing him to be in the company' does not reflect the position of εἶναι.
ASV 'among their kinsfolk and acquaintance' covers both nouns with one 'among'; a repeated ἐν has no separate exponent.
ASV 'when they found him not' needs an object in English regardless, so 'him' does not require an expressed αὐτόν.
ASV 'seeking for him' renders ἀναζητοῦντες and simple ζητοῦντες alike.
Word order only; ASV 'his mother said unto him' does not reflect the position of εἶπεν.
ASV 'thy father and I sought thee sorrowing' is past, rendering the imperfect ἐζητοῦμεν; the present ζητοῦμεν would give 'seek thee'.
ASV 'kept all these sayings' renders ταῦτα; the omission would give 'all the sayings'.

ASV 'advanced in wisdom and stature' fixes the order wisdom-then-stature, excluding Treg's ἡλικίᾳ καὶ σοφίᾳ; the article and ἐν have no exponent in the English, which needs 'in' for the dative in any case.
